slices.focus: Denise nudges Tasha to NC State game; Tasha discovers low-effort social as a restoration format
slices.summary: After work swallows several weekends with volunteer recruiting, Denise overrules Tasha's plan to stay home and brings her to watch an NC State game with family. The evening — cousins, paper plates, casual arguing about calls — turns out to be exactly what Tasha needed. She realizes that shared-attention activities (where the game carries the social atmosphere) are far more restorative than elaborate social plans that require her to organize and perform. The agent helps her see this as a 'default yes-plan' category and a seasonal March ritual worth protecting. Tasha plans to be more intentional about saying yes to low-effort invitations during heavy stretches and to mark NC State games as a recurring spring touchpoint.
open_loops: Tell Denise she was right about the game — planned
Mark March basketball as recurring seasonal ritual — idea only
Develop mental list of default yes-plans (game watch, takeout, porch visit) — to be created
decisions: Tasha became more intentional about catching NC State games with family or friends each March as an easy, low effort soc
